title: SPA/262/2015 of Sher Singh Rawat Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No.262 of 2015
Sher Singh Rawat, ....Appellant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .... Respondents

Present: Mr. Amar Shukla, Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State/respondents.
Date: 15th June 2015
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.

Petitioner has filed the writ petition for the following
reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondents to fix the seniority of the
petitioner from 01.01.1986 in view of
judgment passed by Hon'ble Court in writ
petition no.932 (M/B) 2005 order dated
08.03.2007 passed in Review application
no.83 of 2007 and order dated 14.02.2011
passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
SLP No.CC-1120-1121 of 2011 "State of
Uttaranchal and others vs. Uttarakhand
Shikshak Sangh and others" and in
compliance of government order dated
04.04.2013, 21.11.2006 and issued by the
respondent no.1.
(ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondents to grant the benefit of
seniority, arrears etc. to the petitioner
from the date of dying C.T. Cadre.
(iii) Issue a writ order or direction which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper
under the facts and circumstances of the
case.
(iv) Award the cost of the petition".

2
2. Learned Single Judge declined to interfere in
promotional exercise for the administrative post of Principal, but
sought response from the respondents as regards the denial of the
selection/promotional pay-scale.
3. It is the contention of learned counsel for the appellant
that infact the issue of selection/promotional pay scale was not
settled. He submitted that the learned Single Judge should have
directed the respondents to seek instructions in respect of the prayer
no.1. Since the order passed by the learned Single Judge is
interlocutory order and order has also been passed for listing the
case after six weeks and time for six weeks is going to expire very
soon, we are not inclined to entertain the appeal. The appeal is
dismissed. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that
since the promotional exercise is going to complete, order be
passed for the promotion, which are going to be made, but subject
to the final decision of the writ petition.
4. In our view such order is not required to be passed by
us in appellate stage as every order is subject to the decision of the
writ petition. The apprehension of learned counsel for the appellant
is that the learned Single Judge simply asked instructions in respect
of the selection/promotional pay scale and respondents will not file
counter affidavit to the pleadings of the writ petition. This
apprehension is misconceived. Learned Government Counsel
submits that reply to every paragraph will be given by the
respondents in writ petition.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.) (V.K. Bist, J.)
 15.06.2015 15.06.2015
